title: GPU segmentation and degradation signaling for commitment classes
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Implement a GPU fleet segmentation and automated degradation-signaling system that enforces committed throughput classes while protecting best-effort tenants. This ticket covers: (1) an allocator-based segmentation model for committed vs best-effort slices, (2) quota enforcement and soft-preemption semantics, (3) noisy-client detection and automated attenuation, and (4) a degradation signaling API so downstream applications can gracefully degrade quality or route to fallback models.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Committed slices can reserve throughput with >95% success for steady traffic at target p50 latency; 2) Best-effort tenants are quarantined to soft-attenuation profiles when noisy behavior detected; 3) Token-bucket quotas and burst reservoirs enforce burst isolation with documented burst decay parameters; 4) Degradation signaling endpoint emits standardized JSON events (reason, severity, available_tokens, suggested_fallback_model) and is consumed by at least two internal services; 5) End-to-end load tests demonstrate graceful degradation rather than hard failures under 2x committed demand.
design_notes: Segmentation: Use a two-tier allocation model. Committed slices map to reservation pools with guaranteed token rates. Best-effort runs in a shared reservoir with proportional fairness. Enforcement: Combine cgroups/gpu-manager controls with admission-layer token-bucket per-tenant. Preemption: Implement soft-preemption that reduces concurrency and throttles new requests before evicting active KV caches; hard-preemption reserved for safety-critical SLA violations.
implementation_plan: Phase A: allocator + quota enforcement (cgroups hooks, admission token-bucket). Phase B: telemetry hooks for noisy detection (latency anomaly, GPU util spikes, queue-growth classifier). Phase C: attenuation layer (concurrency caps, model-resolution downgrade / quantized fallback routing), degradation signaling API, and observability dashboards. Phase D: controlled rollout to a single region, then global rollouts with canaries and automatic rollback.
telemetry_and_detection: Signal set includes per-tenant p50/p95 latency, queue depth, GPU SM% and memory pressure, KV cache hit ratio, and inter-request spacing. Noisy neighbor model: gradient-boosted classifier trained on historical incidents (inputs: short-term util delta, error-rate spike, token churn). Thresholds configured per pool with a safety hysteresis window to avoid flapping.
attenuation_strategies: Ordered mitigations: 1) request shaping (enforce inter-request spacing), 2) concurrency caps, 3) automatic model resolution downgrade (float32->int8 or switch to quantized variant), 4) route to lower-cost background pool, 5) eviction of cold KV caches. Each mitigation emits a structured event to degradation signaling so clients can adapt.
quota_specification: Committed pools configured with guaranteed_tokens_per_second and max_burst_tokens. Bursts decay exponentially with half-life configured per customer class. Best-effort reservoir uses a weighted fair share allocator with leak-rate control. Admins can define emergency reserve tokens for healthchecks and control-plane traffic.
degradation_api: HTTP endpoint /v1/tenants/{tenant}/degradation-status returning fields: status, severity, available_tokens, suggestion (fallback model id or target concurrency). Events also stream to telemetry via Kafka topic 'degradation-signals' for downstream automation.
testing_plan: Unit tests for token-bucket correctness, integration tests for admission path with simulated GPUs, chaos tests that inject noisy jobs and verify attenuation ordering, e2e synthetic load tests that assert p95 latency for committed slices stays within SLO under 1.5x baseline load, and soak tests for 72h.
rollout_plan: 1) Internal canary using engineering internal org (5% capacity), 2) Gradual ramp to 20% with smoke gates, 3) Customer canary with two low-risk customers, 4) Full rollout region-by-region. Rollback triggers: more than 10% committed request failures or >2x expected latency p95 for >10 minutes.
metrics_and_dashboards: Add dashboards: per-pool throughput, token utilization, attenuation events per-minute, classifier confidence, and customer-exposed degradation events. SLIs: committed_success_rate, committed_p95_latency, attenuation_event_rate, noisy_classification_false_positive_rate.
security_and_compliance: Degradation API requires tenant-scoped auth tokens. Audit logs retained per enterprise compliance policy. Security review required because quota enforcement touches tenant isolation and KMS-wrapped keys for per-tenant reservation metadata.
